discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological phases of matter
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological insulator, the quantum spin Hall state. They identified a new Z2 topological invariant that separates it from ordinary band insulators and implies protected helical edge states. In 2007 Molenkamp's group observed quantized edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells, the first experimental realization of this phase. Their work turned band topology from a curiosity of the quantum Hall effect into a general organizing principle for crystalline solids. It quickly led to three-dimensional topological insulators, topological crystalline insulators, Weyl semimetals and the quantum anomalous Hall effect. It also gave the field a systematic program for classifying and searching for topological materials, which is now carried out in thousands of compounds. Few ideas in condensed matter have so completely changed what experimentalists look for and what theorists consider a phase of matter.
